prompt:
Build "Storm Rescue — Helicopter over a Raging Sea": a visually stunning, real-time interactive 3D scene delivered as ONE self-contained HTML file.

HARD REQUIREMENTS
- One .html file, no external files, libraries, CDNs, fonts or network requests. Raw WebGL 2 and Web Audio only; all geometry, textures and sounds are generated in code.
- All UI text and buttons in English.
- Must open by double-click in Chrome/Edge and run at 60 fps on an RTX 4070-class GPU at 1440p. Include a Quality button (Low / Medium / High / Ultra) with automatic downgrade if frames get slow.
- Maximum detail and smoothness. No intersecting parts, no z-fighting, nothing overexposed or washed out; rich, saturated but believable colours.

RENDERING
- HDR pipeline (RGBA16F), MSAA, bloom, ACES-style tone mapping, dithering.
- PBR shading (GGX), environment reflections from a sky cubemap re-baked as the clouds move, soft PCF shadow map around the helicopter.
- Everything outdoors is wet: darker, glossier, with water running down the surfaces.

THE STORM SEA — MAKE IT AS REALISTIC AS POSSIBLE
- Open ocean only: no boats, rafts, buoys or debris. The sea itself is the second hero of the scene.
- Many layered Gerstner waves: long heavy swells (up to ~10 m crest to trough in Storm mode) travelling with the wind, medium waves at spread angles, fine wind chop, plus detail normal maps at three scales so the surface never looks smooth or repetitive in close-up. Wave groups: amplitude slowly modulated so sets of bigger waves roll through.
- Sharp steep crests, wide troughs, no visible tiling to the horizon; mesh dense under the camera and stretching to the horizon.
- Breaking crests detected from surface folding: thick foam that appears at the crest, trails down the back of the wave where it broke a moment ago, and old foam laid in long streaks along the wind. Foam pattern must be fine and lacy, not big cells.
- Spindrift: spray torn off the crests and carried downwind.
- Water shading: Fresnel reflection of the storm sky; deep blue-black body; green-teal glow through thin backlit crests; glitter under the break in the clouds; every lamp lights the water and the foam.
- Rain: thousands of tiny impact rings and sparkles on the surface.
- Rotor downwash: a flattened patch under the helicopter with radial ripples and a ring of mist that follows the aircraft.
- The camera never goes under water: at sea level it rides the surface and the waves tower over it.
- Controls: Wave height (Calm / Rough / Storm), changing smoothly.

SKY AND WEATHER
- Heavy layered storm clouds drifting with the wind, a break in the clouds with a dim sun or moon. Time of day button: Dusk / Night / Stormy dawn, each with its own sky, light, water colour and exposure, blending smoothly.
- Rain: wind-driven streaks around the camera, three levels (off / light / heavy), lit by the searchlight where they cross its beam. Fog thickens with rain.
- Realistic lightning: a fractal main channel from the cloud base to the sea with thinner forks peeling off downward, a white-hot core inside a violet corona, a different shape every strike, two or three flickers per strike, clouds lit from inside around the bolt, the whole scene briefly lit WITHOUT blowing out the image. Thunder delayed by distance. Random strikes plus a "Lightning" button.
- A rocky headland in the distance with a lighthouse: rotating beam visible in the rain, surf bursting on the rocks.

THE HELICOPTER — REALISTIC, EVERY DETAIL MODELLED
- Medium twin-engine search-and-rescue helicopter, original design, orange-red livery with white belly, navy cheat line, white and navy diagonal stripes, black anti-glare panel and radome, yellow tail band. No real logos or registrations.
- Correct silhouette: drooping nose with radome, raked windscreen with centre and corner posts, chin windows under the pilots' feet, cabin with framed windows, belly rising into a slim tail boom, swept fin, one-sided horizontal stabiliser, tail bumper.
- Panel seams and rivet lines on the skin, clear-coat reflections.
- Two engines on the roof: intakes with spinners and guide vanes, angled exhausts with dark interiors and heat glow, cooling grilles, gearbox fairing, mast with supports.
- Main rotor: hub with swashplate, pitch links, blade grips with bolts, dampers; 5 blades with real aerofoil section, twist, swept tips, yellow and red tip bands. Tail rotor with 4 blades, hub and pitch links. At full speed the rotors read as a faint disc with soft ghost blades; in slow motion the solid blades are visible.
- Sponsons with float packs; retractable landing gear with oleo struts, torque links, brake lines, wheels with hubs.
- Rescue hoist on a boom above the starboard door with drum and hook; sliding side door on rails with a window and handle.
- Nose FLIR turret, gimballed searchlight with finned body and reflector, antennas, pitot tubes, wire cutters, wipers, steps, handholds.
- Cockpit: instrument panel with glowing multi-colour displays and glare shield, centre console, overhead panel, cyclic and collective sticks, pedals, crash-worthy seats with cushions and headrests.
- Cabin: troop seats, stretcher with a blanket, medical kit, oxygen bottle, winch control pendant, red cabin lights.
- Flight behaviour: hovers nose into the wind with constant small pitch/roll/yaw corrections against gusts.

HIGH-QUALITY LIGHTS
- Every lamp is a real lamp: lens geometry plus a glow sprite with a hot core, soft halo and a four-point star, sized with distance so it reads from far away.
- Green and red navigation lights, white tail light, red anti-collision beacons with a real double-flash strobe pattern, white strobe on the stabiliser, two landing lights on the nose, hoist lamp, the swimmer's blinking marker light, the lighthouse lantern.
- Searchlight: bright moving pool on the water, visible beam cone in the rain and spray, and it dazzles when you look into it.

PEOPLE — DETAILED AND REALISTIC
- Built from proper anatomy: hips, waist, ribcage, shoulders, neck; head with jaw, nose, ears, eyes; arms and legs with tapering muscles, knees and elbows; hands with four fingers and a thumb; boots with soles.
- Two pilots in flight suits, helmets with dark visors, ear cups, chin straps and boom mics, survival vests, hands on the controls.
- Hoist operator kneeling in the open door in an orange suit, helmet, harness with a safety strop to the roof.
- Rescue swimmer in an orange dry suit with reflective tape, yellow helmet, harness, fins, marker light.
- Survivor in oilskins with a life vest and hood, hanging limp in the rescue sling.

THE RESCUE — EVERY ACTION ANIMATED
- "Rescue sequence" button runs the full 32-second operation: door slides open → swimmer steps out on the hook → cable pays out while he swings and slowly spins in the wind and downwash → enters the water with a splash → swims to the survivor → fits the sling → both are winched up, swinging in then settling → pulled into the cabin → door closes.
- The survivor is only in the water while a rescue is running; otherwise the sea is empty.
- The cable is a real curved line that bows in the wind and goes slack in the water, never a straight stick.
- The searchlight tracks the swimmer the whole time.
- "Hoist" button does the same by hand in two stages: lower and hold, then raise.

FUNCTIONS (buttons in a left column with key badges, each with its own sound)
- Rescue sequence, Hoist lower/raise, Searchlight, Side door, Landing gear, Rotor slow-mo (shows blades and hub mechanics), Lightning, Rain (off/light/heavy), Waves (calm/rough/storm), Night vision (green image-intensifier look with grain and a round tube), Fly-by, Exploded view (fuselage, glazing, engines, rotor system, tail rotor, interior with crew, door, hoist, searchlight, gear separated).
- Fly-by must look like real flying: one wide banked orbit over the sea lasting about 18 seconds, easing gently out of the hover and back into it, bank angle derived from speed and turn rate, nose down while accelerating and up while slowing, no jerks or snaps anywhere.

CAMERA
- Orbit camera with inertia: drag to orbit, scroll/pinch to zoom, right-drag or Shift+drag to pan; double-click resets. The camera target follows the helicopter, the swimmer or the lighthouse depending on the view.
- 10 named viewpoints with smooth eased fly-to transitions (no jumps), number keys 1–0: Hero shot, Cockpit, Pilots, Rotor head, Hoist, Open door, Top down, Sea level, Lighthouse, Wide storm.
- Auto-rotate when idle; Hide UI; Fullscreen.

SOUND (Web Audio, synthesised, starts on first click)
- Rotor blade thump and turbine whine that follow rotor speed and camera distance, wind, rain, heavy sea, thunder with distance delay, hoist motor, door, landing gear, splash, radio beeps, lighthouse foghorn.
- A tense cinematic music loop at 96 BPM; the music must sit slightly above the ambient layers. Separate Music and Sound toggles.

DEMO
- "Demo 19s" button (key D): 18.75 seconds, hard cuts on the bars of the music, UI hidden, any click or key cancels, state restored afterwards. No exploded view in the demo. Shots:
1. The storm with a lightning strike, helicopter coming out of it.
2. Sweep round the nose into the cockpit with the pilots and glowing instruments.
3. Sweep round the tail to the open side.
4. Door open, swimmer goes down the wire in the searchlight beam.
5. Sea level: swimmer and survivor in the pool of light, waves towering.
6. Both winched up through a lightning strike.
7. The helicopter banks away into the cloud, another strike, fade out.
- "Record demo" button (Shift+D): records the same demo with sound to a .webm file using MediaRecorder.

UI
- Clean, minimal, semi-transparent panels: title top-left, function buttons in a left column, viewpoints along the bottom, toggles top-right, a one-line controls hint.
- Loading screen with progress text; friendly error if WebGL 2 is unavailable.

QUALITY BAR
- Treat it as a portfolio showpiece. The sea must look like real storm footage from every angle; the helicopter must hold up in extreme close-ups of the cockpit, rotor hub and hoist; every action must animate smoothly with easing and physical weight.
- Check every viewpoint and every function state for clipping, intersections, overexposure and unreadable dark areas before finishing.
